traits.label: Delegates tactical decisions
traits.text: Longstreet defers to General Lee's prior rejection of a flanking maneuver, instructing General Hood that the move had been considered and rejected by their chief.

citation.doc: Longstreet, From Manassas to Appomattox (1896), ch. XXVII (scan)
citation.quote: the move to the right had been carefully considered by our chief and rejected in favor of his present orders

traits.label: Critiques superior's absence
traits.text: Longstreet argues that General Lee's failure to be present on the field prevented the proper adjustment of the battle to difficult terrain and the adoption of a better opportunity.

citation.doc: Longstreet, From Manassas to Appomattox (1896), ch. XXVII (scan)
citation.quote: leaving the battle to be adjusted to formidable and difficult grounds without his assistance

traits.label: Enforces strict obedience
traits.text: Longstreet characterizes the act of sending messengers to headquarters to propose a previously rejected move as contumacious, emphasizing the necessity of adhering to existing orders.

citation.doc: Longstreet, From Manassas to Appomattox (1896), ch. XXVII (scan)
citation.quote: to delay and send messengers five miles in favor of a move that he had rejected would have been contumacious

traits.label: Cautious under pressure
traits.text: Longstreet delays his attack until his forces are fully assembled, fearing his current strength is insufficient to succeed.

citation.doc: Longstreet's report, July 27, 1863 (Official Records, Ser. I, Vol. 27, Part 2, scan)
citation.quote: Fearing that my force was too weak to venture to make an attack, I delayed until General Law's brigade joined its division.

traits.label: Prudent in retreat
traits.text: He chooses to halt his advance and consolidate his position rather than pushing further when his left flank becomes exposed.

citation.doc: Longstreet's report, July 27, 1863 (Official Records, Ser. I, Vol. 27, Part 2, scan)
citation.quote: I thought it prudent not to push farther until my other troops came up.
